styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Senso-ji, Meiji Jingu and the old low-city lanes.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Sushi counters, ramen shops and izakaya alleys.

styles.label: Anime
styles.blurb: Akihabara, Nakano Broadway and themed cafés.

stays.why: Biggest train hub, endless food and nightlife, easy day trips west. Busy and bright at night.
Central for youth culture, shopping and nightlife. Good links to Shinjuku and the west side.
Quiet, polished and walkable; best for Shinkansen day trips and first-time comfort.
Cheapest rooms, old-town feel, Senso-ji on the doorstep and good airport links.

food: Try sushi at a conveyor-belt shop for a cheap first taste; sit-down counters cost much more. Check prices before you sit.
Ramen and standing soba shops are the cheap lunch: expect roughly ¥800–1,300 a bowl.
Izakaya alleys (Omoide Yokocho in Shinjuku, Harmonica Yokocho in Kichijoji) are best for small plates and a beer.
Convenience stores (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) are good, cheap breakfasts and picnic food.
Many small restaurants are cash-only and some are ticket-machine only. Carry some yen and have a translation app ready.
more_time: Add a day trip to Nikko or Kamakura by train; both are easy returns from central stations. Check times on the day.
Swap one city day for teamLab or a sumo morning session (tickets sell out; check the schedule).
Anime fans can swap a shopping afternoon for Nakano Broadway and a themed café; book popular cafés ahead.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the big sights, a food neighbourhood and one day trip without rushing.

month_notes: Cold and dry: highs near 9°C, lows around 0°C. Pack a warm coat.
Still cold, highs near 10°C. A few rainy days; keep indoor plans ready.
Warming up to 14°C. Cherry blossom timing varies; check forecasts on the day.
Mild and pleasant at 19°C. Busy blossom season; book hotels early.
Warm at 23°C and green. Good walking weather before the rains.
Rainy season: about 15 rain days and 26°C. Carry an umbrella.
Hot and humid, highs near 30°C with 16 rain days. Plan indoor breaks.
Hottest month, highs near 31°C. Go out early and late; stay cool midday.
Still warm at 27°C with 15 rain days. Typhoon season; check forecasts.
Comfortable at 22°C. Great month for walking and day trips.
Cool and clear at 17°C. Autumn colours; popular, so book ahead.
Cold again at 11°C. Dry with about 7 rain days; pack layers.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold dry winters, a humid rainy season in June, and hot, sticky summers.

items.title: Best time: March to May and October to November
items.text: Mild days around 17–23°C. Ideal for walking neighbourhoods and day trips.

items.title: Summer is hot and humid (July to September)
items.text: Highs near 30–31°C with muggy nights. Plan indoor sights midday and go out early or late.

items.title: Rainy season in June
items.text: About 15 rain days and 26°C. Carry an umbrella and keep a museum or shopping backup.

items.title: Cold, dry winters
items.text: January highs near 9°C and lows around 0°C. A warm coat and layers matter; rain is light.

items.title: Typhoon season
items.text: Late summer and September can bring storms. Check forecasts and train status on the day.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes, layers for cool evenings, an umbrella in June and September, and light breathable clothes in summer.

transit.best: Trains and subways with an IC card; taxis only for late nights.

modes.text: JR, Tokyo Metro and Toei reach everywhere. Tap a Suica or Pasmo IC card, about ¥180–330 a ride.
Same network as the metro for visitors; use it between neighbourhoods. Trains stop around midnight.
Buses exist but trains are almost always faster for visitors.
Clean and metered, ¥500 start. Apps like GO and Uber work. Best after the trains stop.
Driving in central Tokyo is slow and parking expensive; not recommended.
Each neighbourhood is walkable, but you will take trains between them.
